recipes.name: Portobello Mushroom Burgers
ingredients_raw: lettuce, tomato, and red onion for serving

steps.text: Place mushroom caps, smooth side up, in a shallow dish.
Whisk together balsamic, oil, garlic, basil, and oregano in a small bowl. Season with salt and pepper.
Pour vinaigrette over mushrooms. Let stand at room temperature for 15 minutes or so, turning twice. Preheat grill for medium-high heat.
Brush grill grates with oil. Place mushrooms on grill, reserving marinade for basting.
Grill until just tender, 5 to 8 minutes per side, brushing with marinade frequently.
Continue grilling until cheese is melted, about 2 minutes.
Serve in buns with lettuce, tomato, and red onion, or your favorite toppings. Enjoy!

raw_recipe.headline: Portobello Mushroom Burgers
raw_recipe.description: This meaty portobello mushroom burger has a juicy grilled, marinated mushroom, topped with melty cheese, served in a bun with your favorite toppings.

video.description: In this video, learn how to make portobello mushroom burgers, the steak of veggie burgers. This classic vegetarian recipe will make meatless Mondays in your house a highlight. Use large, fresh mushroom caps that have been thoroughly cleaned for the best results. This dish comes together quickly, and it only takes about a half hour to make. Serve these flavor-packed caps on buns with lettuce, tomato, and aioli sauce.

review.reviewBody:
This recipe is excellent. However, I don't have a grill so the first time I broiled them on a cookie sheet with tin foil. They came out great, but I found that the marinated made them slightly runny. Next time I made them I placed them on a wire rack with a cookie sheet under it and broiled it for the same amount of time - about 5 minutes on both sides. Came out fantastic!
Update: I've made these burgers so many times now, they're that good. To add some extra flavour, chop 2-3 onions and sauté them for at least 20 minutes on low heat with olive oil and butter. Viola, caramelized onions, which taste AMAZING with these burgers. One final note for those who didn't like the vinegar taste: a good balsamic is essential. The cheap stuff (under 5 bucks) is gross and overpowering. Buy a good bottle (you'll use less) and it tastes much sweeter.
Wow! The cheese really makes this a treat. I tried grilling this on my Foreman grill for just a few minutes, and it comes out perfect!

After reading all the comments, I got a great result from the following tweaks (based on 3 portobellos) Used 2 TBSP each of oil and white balsamic, plus all other ingredients as listed. Removed gills, salted each mushroom generously, and pricked with a fork. Marinated 5 minutes each side. Topped with grated parmesan and diced cherry tomatoes. Baked at 375 for 15 minutes, added provolone till melted.

Amazing! I didn't grill it because I was too lazy to get the grill out. I put it in the oven at high heat. I added cheese and bacon. ??. It was amazing. I think I had a PMBurger once or twice before, it was okay. This one was juicy and didn't taste like meat. It became it's own thing. I wouldn't call it a burger because it didn't have to imitate anything - It stood alone on it's own merit! I'm eating the left over for lunch.

Just looking for something different as I've got a bad case of the Sheltering Blues. 

Changed things up a bit here. Marinated for but half the time cited in the recipe. Carmelized vidalia onion and topped off the burger with smoked applewood gouda. 

Also used some lobster claw meat which, after cleaning, dropped into drawn butter with fresh tarragon, which I then topped the burger with for an open face burger.

A bit more intensive, but worth the effort. Effort is always rewarded.

I used my George Forman grill to do this... @300 for 8 minutes... opening every two minutes to put on the marinade... very good ... I used the STAR brand from Fred Meyer for the vinegar and I thought it tasted great .. I didn't use bread buns I used lettuce to wrap the mushroom up ... very good enjoyed doing this and I will for sure use this recipe again

I loved these! I marinated the mushrooms for about an hour (gills removed) and added a bit of liquid smoke to the mixture. I had mine on Romaine "buns" with regular toppings and grilled onions and peppers!

I loved this! I made a few changes to the marinade, but I am sure it is fine as written. I used fresh basil instead of dried, added 1/5 of an onion, and the stems of the mushrooms. I placed all the ingredients into the food processor to make the marinade. I then let the mushrooms sit in the marinade for a full hour. I used another reviewer's suggestion and caramelized onions in the pan while the mushrooms marinated, and they were the perfect topping for the sandwich. Subbed goat cheese for provolone and used a cast iron grill pan instead of the outdoor grill.

We LOVE this recipe. We are constantly making these. We also do not use a grill but instead use either my griddle pan or fry pan. Either way, they are so delicious! We also like to add a slice of red onion to each. We forgot to melt the cheese this time but they were still just as tasty. What an amazing way to eat these portabellas!

Loved these. My wife felt the vinegar was a little too much for mushroom flavor so will do more olive oil next time. Concerned that the garlic might be too much, so added just a little less, but barely tasted it (the minced garlic stays on top of the gills, so adding the cheese smoothed out the flavor). Grilled with gill side down first, then after turning, added blue cheese during last two minutes - very good.

I have made these several times we love them I use fresh basil and oregano in marinade also added a bit of liquid smoke and Worcestershire I have topped with provolone caramelized onions you can use pretty much what ever cheese you like we have used gouda also love them I have grilled outside and also in oven turn out perfect a little hint take a fork and poke them while grilling they won't be as soggy
These were SO GOOD!

I don't know why so many people rave about this. It was OK, not great. The marinade dribbles and seeps out of the mushroom when you bite into it and soaks the bottom bun. The top of the mushroom has a tough skin which is hard to bite through, so the whole thing tries to come out with every bite. Or maybe it's just me. My daughter, who has a tendency to drop food on the floor a lot, managed to get through the whole thing without making a mess.
Was super surprised with this one! I was a bit sceptical , but it was amazing! Will do again
Didn’t use a grill made in the oven, probably better on a grill but I don’t have one
Delicious! We substituted with caramelized onion cheddar and smoked cheddar.

Very tasty and a great vegan/gluten free recipe. This is a very healthy grilling alternative to a hamburger; which we still love to grill. The marinade and provolone makes this an awesome alternative. This is part of our summertime meal choices!
I'm made this recipe so many times. So incredibly simple and delicious!
Absolutely delicious even managed to get my kid to each one and he hates mushrooms.
Delicious with or without cheese.
